claims: Alzheimer's is a progressive, incurable brain disorder.
Alzheimer's is the most common cause of dementia.
Alzheimer's affects memory, thinking, and behavior.
Alzheimer's typically impacts adults over 65.
Symptoms of Alzheimer's worsen over time from mild memory loss to an inability to perform daily tasks.
No cure exists for Alzheimer's.
Lecanemab can help manage symptoms of Alzheimer's.
Donanemab can help manage symptoms of Alzheimer's.
Memory loss disrupting daily life is an early sign of Alzheimer's.
Challenges in planning or solving problems is an early sign of Alzheimer's.
Confusion with time or place is an early sign of Alzheimer's.
Language difficulties is an early sign of Alzheimer's.
Misplacing items is an early sign of Alzheimer's.
Mood or personality changes is an early sign of Alzheimer's.
Alzheimer's is caused by the abnormal buildup of proteins in the brain.
Amyloid plaques form between cells.
Tau tangles form within cells.
Amyloid plaques and tau tangles damage neurons.
Amyloid plaques and tau tangles disrupt communication.
Amyloid plaques and tau tangles cause brain cells to die.
Brain cell death in Alzheimer's often starts in the hippocampus.
Age is the greatest risk factor for Alzheimer's.
Risk of Alzheimer's increases after 65.
Family history can influence risk of Alzheimer's.
The mild stage of Alzheimer's is the early stage.
Individuals in the mild stage of Alzheimer's may function independently.
Individuals in the mild stage of Alzheimer's experience memory lapses.
The moderate stage of Alzheimer's is the middle stage.
The moderate stage of Alzheimer's is the longest stage.
The moderate stage of Alzheimer's requires more care.
Confusion becomes more pronounced in the moderate stage of Alzheimer's.
Behavior changes become more pronounced in the moderate stage of Alzheimer's.
Memory loss becomes more pronounced in the moderate stage of Alzheimer's.
The severe stage of Alzheimer's is the late stage.
Individuals in the severe stage of Alzheimer's lose the ability to respond to their environment.
Individuals in the severe stage of Alzheimer's lose the ability to carry on a conversation.
Individuals in the severe stage of Alzheimer's eventually lose control of movement.
Symptoms of late-onset Alzheimer's become apparent after age 65.
Symptoms of early-onset Alzheimer's occur before age 65.
Early-onset Alzheimer's is rare.
